sections.heading: Comparatives
sections.body: We use comparatives to compare two things or people. There are two forms: short adjectives add -er, long adjectives use 'more'.

sections.heading: Short adjectives
table: My house is bigger than yours.
This test is easier than the last one.

sections.heading: Long adjectives
table: She is more beautiful than her sister.

sections.heading: Irregular comparatives
table: This film is better than that one.
The station is further than I thought.

sections.heading: Superlatives
sections.body: Superlatives compare one thing with all the others in a group. Short adjectives: the + -est. Long adjectives: the most + adjective.
table: He is the tallest in the class.
This is the most interesting book.

sections.heading: Countable and uncountable nouns
sections.body: Countable nouns can be counted (one apple, two apples). Uncountable nouns cannot (water, money, rice).
list: Countable: apple, book, chair, friend, car
Uncountable: water, milk, rice, money, time, information
We use 'many' with countable, 'much' with uncountable.
We use 'a few' with countable, 'a little' with uncountable.

sections.heading: Some and any
list: Some: positive sentences. There is some milk.
Any: negatives and questions. There isn't any milk. Is there any milk?

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'more' with short adjectives: 'more tall' is wrong. Say 'taller'.
Do not use -er with long adjectives: 'interestinger' is wrong. Say 'more interesting'.
Do not confuse 'much' and 'many': much + uncountable, many + countable.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: My car is faster than yours.
This is the biggest city in the country.
The film was more interesting than the book.
She is the most intelligent student in the class.
This book is better than that one.
There is some milk in the fridge.
questions: In sentences 1 and 3, how do we form the comparative of 'fast' and 'interesting'?
In sentences 2 and 4, how do we form the superlative?
In sentences 6 and 7, when do we use 'some' and when 'any'?
In sentence 8, why do we use 'many' instead of 'much'?

questions.prompt: This book is ___ than that one.
questions.explanation: For long adjectives we use more + adjective + than.

questions.prompt: She is the ___ student in the class.
questions.explanation: Good is irregular. Its superlative is 'best'.

questions.prompt: My brother is ___ than me.
This is the ___ restaurant in town.
questions.explanation: Long adjective superlative: the most + adjective.

questions.prompt: There is ___ milk in the fridge.
Are there ___ apples?
How ___ money do you have?
questions.explanation: Money is uncountable, so we use 'how much'.

questions.prompt: How ___ students are there?
questions.explanation: Students is countable, so we use 'how many'.

questions.prompt: This dress is ___ than that one.
That was the ___ film I have ever seen.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Compare two cities you know. Write 5 sentences using comparatives and superlatives (bigger, more beautiful, the most expensive, etc.).
Compare your house with a friend's house. Write 5 sentences about size, rooms and garden.
Write 5 sentences comparing two foods you like (pizza vs pasta, coffee vs tea, etc.).

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Short adjectives: add -er (taller, bigger) and -est (the tallest).
Long adjectives: use more + adjective and the most + adjective.
Irregular: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst.
Comparatives use 'than': She is taller than me.
Superlatives use 'the': She is the tallest.
Countable: many, a few. Uncountable: much, a little.
Some: positive. Any: negatives and questions.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'more' with short adjectives.
Do not use -er with long adjectives.
Do not mix 'much' and 'many'.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: ... is bigger than ...
... is the most ...
How much...?
How many...?
There is some...
Are there any...?
